open_questions_for_vendor: Please confirm the exact current legal entity that contracts for the Replicate service (name, legal form, state of formation, and registered address) following the Cloudflare acquisition — is it Replicate, LLC, and is it a wholly-owned subsidiary of Cloudflare, Inc.? Your public pages show two addresses (101 Townsend Street, San Francisco, CA 94107 on replicate.com/privacy; 2261 Market Street #4056, San Francisco, CA 94114 on internal.replicate.com/privacy) — which is authoritative?
Has Replicate (or its Cloudflare parent, on Replicate's behalf) designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Replicate have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm privacy@replicate.com as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests.

Which security certifications or audit reports does Replicate currently hold (SOC 2 Type II, SOC 1/3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27018, 27701, 22301, 9001)? Please provide the current reports/certificates. If Replicate is now covered under Cloudflare, Inc.'s compliance program, please state which certifications extend to the Replicate service and from what date.
What minimum TLS version is enforced for data in transit (a) on the public API endpoints (api.replicate.com) and (b) for internal traffic between services and model pods?

Is customer data (prediction inputs, outputs, files, logs, custom model weights) encrypted at rest, with which algorithm (e.g. AES-256), and on which underlying cloud provider(s) and region(s) is it stored?
Are backups of customer data taken, and if so are they encrypted and with which algorithm?
Who generates and manages the encryption keys for data at rest — Replicate/its cloud provider (shared or customer-specific keys), or can customers supply their own keys (CMEK/BYOK)?

Can Replicate anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data on the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support), as opposed to the aggregated/anonymized 'Resultant Data' described in your Terms?

Does Replicate offer an EU processing region or EU data residency option (inference executed and data stored within the EU/EEA)? If yes, how is it enabled and does it cover video/audio inference workloads?

Please provide your current sub-processor list (your docs reference replicate.com/docs/topics/site-policy/subprocessors) so the full processing chain (Level 2: underlying cloud/GPU providers) can be reported to SAP.
